summary: The bill amends the Clean Air Act to narrow New Source Review permitting by redefining a modification as only a change that raises a source's maximum hourly emission rate of any pollutant, excluding efficiency/safety/reliability projects unless they cause adverse health or environmental effects, and limiting required preconstruction permits to physical construction of discrete emissions-unit parts rather than other on-site activities.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends Clean Air Act definitions related to permitting for stationary sources. It contains no provisions affecting federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses air pollution permitting and has no connection to health insurance, medical services, or healthcare delivery systems.
No references to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill is silent on immigration, border policy, or related legal pathways.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy provisions.

The bill directly narrows the definitions of 'modification' and 'construction' under the Clean Air Act's New Source Review program. It exempts efficiency, reliability, safety, and certain pollution-control projects from triggering permitting requirements unless the EPA finds an adverse health or environmental effect. This reduces the regulatory burden on stationary sources and limits the reach of environmental permitting rules.
